dataset: Codex Conditions official shoulder-knee etiology B15
policy: Fill only currently empty bilingual etiology fields for four mechanical shoulder or knee Conditions. Preserve all existing canonical pathology, risk factors, red flags, scope, relations, and provenance; append direct orthopedic-society or hospital sources. Distinguish structural findings from symptomatic causation and avoid a single-mechanism account when the condition is heterogeneous.

cond.shoulder_instability.etiology_zh: 肩關節不穩定可由不同機轉造成。最常見的是初次創傷性半脫位或脫位拉伸、撕裂或剝離關節囊、盂肱韌帶與關節唇；組織若在鬆弛位置癒合，之後每次再脫位又可累積軟組織及骨性損傷，形成復發性不穩。反覆投擲或其他過頭活動也可由微創傷逐漸拉鬆關節囊。另有無明顯外傷的多方向不穩定，與先天囊袋較寬、全身韌帶鬆弛或結締組織遺傳疾病相關。必須依創傷史、方向、隨意控制能力與是否全身鬆弛分類，不能把所有肩痛或影像上的 labral 改變都等同臨床不穩。
cond.shoulder_instability.etiology_en: Shoulder instability has several mechanisms. Most commonly, an initial traumatic subluxation or dislocation stretches, tears, or detaches the capsule, glenohumeral ligaments, and labrum; healing in a lax position and tissue or bone damage from subsequent episodes can produce recurrent instability. Repetitive throwing or other overhead activity may gradually stretch the capsule through accumulated microtrauma. Atraumatic multidirectional instability can instead reflect a congenitally capacious capsule, generalized ligamentous laxity, or an inherited connective-tissue disorder. Etiology should be classified by trauma history, direction, voluntary control, and generalized laxity; shoulder pain or a labral imaging finding alone is not equivalent to clinical instability.

etiology_en: AAOS OrthoInfo: Chronic Shoulder Instability — traumatic dislocation, recurrent tissue damage, and capsular laxity (retrieved 2026-08); HSS: Shoulder Separation and Dislocation — single trauma versus accumulated microtrauma (retrieved 2026-08)

cond.subacromial_impingement.etiology_zh: 肩峰下疼痛／夾擠表現通常是多因素造成：旋轉肌腱或肩峰下滑囊在反覆過頭負荷、急性刺激或年齡相關磨損下腫脹、敏感化，抬臂時在肩峰下空間承受壓迫與摩擦。肩峰形態、骨贅、姿勢與肩胛—肱骨運動控制可能改變局部負荷，但不能僅憑其中一項影像發現證明疼痛來源。症狀可突然或逐漸出現，且旋轉肌撕裂、頸源性疼痛、關節炎等可有相似表現；因此「夾擠」應視為臨床症候群描述，而非每一病例都由單一骨性壓迫造成。
cond.subacromial_impingement.etiology_en: Subacromial pain or impingement is usually multifactorial. Repetitive overhead load, acute irritation, or age-related wear can make the rotator-cuff tendon or subacromial bursa swollen and pain-sensitive, increasing compression and friction beneath the acromion during elevation. Acromial shape, osteophytes, posture, and scapulohumeral motor control may modify local load, but no single imaging feature proves the source of pain. Onset may be sudden or gradual, and rotator-cuff tear, cervical referral, arthritis, and other disorders can look similar; “impingement” is therefore a clinical syndrome description rather than proof of one bony-pinching mechanism in every case.

etiology_en: AAOS OrthoInfo: Shoulder Impingement/Rotator Cuff Tendinitis — overhead load, tendon/bursal irritation, anatomy, and wear (retrieved 2026-08); NHS: Shoulder impingement — irritation, injury, wear, and differential warning (last reviewed 2024-11-26)

cond.shoulder_labral_tear.etiology_zh: 肩關節唇損傷的機轉依部位而異。急性跌倒以手撐地、肩部脫位、手臂被強力牽拉或過頭快速發力，可使 labrum 自關節盂邊緣撕離；Bankart 損傷常由脫位時肱骨頭牽拉前下方關節唇造成。SLAP 損傷涉及上方關節唇與肱二頭肌長頭附著處，可由急性牽拉，也可由投擲、舉重等反覆過頭負荷形成。隨年齡增加的磨耗與邊緣毛糙亦很常見，且可能沒有症狀；因此影像發現須與外傷史、疼痛位置、不穩定或卡鎖表現對照。
cond.shoulder_labral_tear.etiology_en: The mechanism of a shoulder labral tear depends on its location. A fall on an outstretched arm, shoulder dislocation, forceful traction, or rapid overhead loading can detach the labrum from the glenoid rim; a Bankart lesion commonly occurs when the humeral head pulls on the anteroinferior labrum during dislocation. A SLAP lesion involves the superior labrum and long-head biceps anchor and may follow acute traction or repetitive overhead loading from throwing or weightlifting. Age-related fraying and degeneration are also common and may be asymptomatic, so imaging must be correlated with trauma history, pain location, instability, or true mechanical catching.

etiology_zh: AAOS OrthoInfo: SLAP Tears — acute, repetitive overhead, and age-related mechanisms (retrieved 2026-08); HSS: Shoulder Labrum Tear — SLAP, Bankart, traumatic, and repetitive mechanisms (updated 2025-05-29)
etiology_en: AAOS OrthoInfo: SLAP Tears — acute, repetitive overhead, and age-related mechanisms (retrieved 2026-08); HSS: Shoulder Labrum Tear — SLAP, Bankart, traumatic, and repetitive mechanisms (updated 2025-05-29)

cond.patellar_tendinopathy.etiology_zh: 髕腱病的確切起始機轉仍未完全釐清，核心是髕腱承受的負荷超過當下適應與修復能力。跳躍、跑步、深蹲或下坡等反覆高負荷，訓練量或強度突然增加，或休息後過快恢復活動，都可造成累積性微損傷；持續負荷下，腱纖維重塑失衡並可出現增厚與結構改變。這不是單純一次急性發炎，也不只等於「運動太多」：長期去負荷後的低容量、恢復不足及全身性代謝或藥物因素亦會影響腱的承載能力。影像結構變化須與局部負荷相關疼痛及臨床檢查對照。
cond.patellar_tendinopathy.etiology_en: The initiating mechanism of patellar tendinopathy is not fully understood, but the central problem is load exceeding the tendon's current capacity to adapt and repair. Repeated high load from jumping, running, squatting, or downhill activity, a rapid increase in training volume or intensity, or an overly rapid return after rest can produce cumulative microdamage; continued loading may lead to disordered remodeling, thickening, and structural change. It is not simply a single episode of acute inflammation or merely “too much exercise”: low capacity after prolonged unloading, inadequate recovery, and systemic metabolic or medication factors can also reduce load tolerance. Imaging changes must be correlated with localized load-related pain and examination findings.
